Patch release of the AnonRouter SDKs, keeping Tinfoil verification current
without weakening the provider trust boundary.

## Packages

| Package | Registry plan |
| --- | --- |
| `@anonrouter/confidential` | npm |
| `@anonrouter/client` | npm |
| `anonrouter-confidential` | GitHub wheel/sdist now; PyPI after organization approval |

The npm and PyPI jobs remain separate release switches. PyPI publication stays
off while the AnonRouter organization request is pending.

## What changed

Tinfoil rotates its signed router release more frequently than AnonRouter ships
SDK updates. The previous SDK copied each accepted release fingerprint into a
second static list, so a valid Tinfoil rollout could make its routes appear
unverified until the next AnonRouter release.

`v0.1.2` replaces that redundant list with a fixed provider-authority policy.
The official verifier must still validate the exact
`tinfoilsh/confidential-model-router` repository, tagged GitHub/Sigstore
release, hardware evidence, signed code equality with the live enclave, and TLS
key binding. A wrong repository, unsigned or malformed release identity,
code-to-enclave mismatch, or TLS-key substitution fails closed.

The JavaScript wrapper now uses the current `tinfoil` 1.2.1 verifier API. The
Python SDK validates the same gateway-supplied verification document and policy;
Python callers who want to run Tinfoil's verifier independently can use
Tinfoil's Python client directly.

AnonRouter's gateway pins, other providers' verification policies, and inference
protocols are unchanged. See
[`docs/release-readiness.md`](https://github.com/anonrouter/anonrouter-sdk/blob/main/docs/release-readiness.md)
for the complete gate results and limitations.
